questions.question: What do you mean by goods repossesed? How are they treated in the books of hire vendor?
questions.solution_html:
• When goods are sold under a hire purchase agreement, ownership remains with the hire vendor
  • until all instalments are paid by the hire purchaser. If the purchaser fails to pay the instalments on
  • time, the vendor has the legal right to take back the goods. This act of taking back the goods is known
  • as repossession of goods. Repossession of goods may be Complete repossession or Partial
  • repossession. ( (2 marks))
  • Accounting treatment in the books of Hire Vendor
  • A) Complete repossession ( (3 marks))
  • In the case of full/complete repossession, the vendor takes back all the goods sold on hire
  • purchase. The goods taken back are recorded in the vendor’s books at their estimated or agreed
  • value, which represents their fair value after considering depreciation or wear and tear.
  • Goods Repossessed or Repossessed Stock A/c Dr.
  • To Hire Purchaser’s A/c
  • If any repair or reconditioning expenses are incurred on the repossessed goods, they are debited to
  • the Goods Repossessed Account. When these goods are later sold, the amount realised is credited to
  • the same account. The difference between the total cost of the goods repossessed (including
  • expenses) and the sale proceeds represents a profit or loss, which is transferred to the Profit and Loss
  • Account.
  • B) Partial Repossession ((2 marks))
  • In the case of partial repossession, the vendor takes back only a portion of the goods. The
  • repossessed portion is valued at an agreed value between the parties and debited to the Goods
  • Repossessed Account, while the same amount is credited to the Hire Purchaser’s Account. The
  • balance still due from the purchaser after such adjustment is either collected in cash or written off
  • as a loss.
questions.final_answer: Option Complete repossession ( (3 marks))

questions.question: Explain the following terms: a) Hire Purchase agreement b) Hire Purchaser c) Cash Price d) Hire Purchase Price e) Cash Price f) Cash Down Payment
questions.solution_html:
• a) Hire Purchase Agreement means an agreement under which goods are let on hire and under
  • which the hirer has an option to purchase them in accordance with the terms of agreement and
  • includes the agreement under which: possession of goods is delivered by the owner there of to a
  • person on a condition that such person pays the agreed amount in periodical instalments, property to
  • pass on to the buyer only on payment of last instalment and such person has right to terminate the
  • agreement at any time before the property passes.
  • b) Hire purchaser: A person who obtains or has obtained possession of goods from an owner under
  • hire purchase agreement is known as hire purchaser or hirer.
  • c)Cash Price: It is the price at which goods may be purchased by the hirer for cash .It is the amount for
  • which an article can be purchased immediately by making a lumpsum payment, without there being
  • the facility of instalment purchase.
  • d) Hire Purchase Price: The total amount that the hire purchaser is required to pay to the hire vendor
  • under the terms of hire purchase contract. The amount includes interest also. It is always higher than
  • cash price of the goods. Hire Purchase Price= Cash Price +Interest.

  • the amount for which an article can be purchased immediately by making a lumpsum payment

  • f) Cash Down Payment: Under the hire purchase system and instalment system, the purchaser is
  • required to pay an amount at the time of signing the agreement. It is called “Down Payment”. It simply
  • means the initial payment made at the time of signing the agreement. It is a part of hire purchase

questions.question: What do you mean by goods repossesed? How are they treated in the books of hire vendor?
questions.solution_html:
• When goods are sold under a hire purchase agreement, ownership remains with the hire vendor
  • until all instalments are paid by the hire purchaser. If the purchaser fails to pay the instalments on
  • time, the vendor has the legal right to take back the goods. This act of taking back the goods is known
  • as repossession of goods. Repossession of goods may be Complete repossession or Partial
  • repossession. ( (2 marks))
  • Accounting treatment in the books of Hire Vendor
  • A) Complete repossession ( (3 marks))
  • In the case of full/complete repossession, the vendor takes back all the goods sold on hire
  • purchase. The goods taken back are recorded in the vendor’s books at their estimated or agreed
  • value, which represents their fair value after considering depreciation or wear and tear.
  • Goods Repossessed or Repossessed Stock A/c Dr.
  • To Hire Purchaser’s A/c
  • If any repair or reconditioning expenses are incurred on the repossessed goods, they are debited to
  • the Goods Repossessed Account. When these goods are later sold, the amount realised is credited to
  • the same account. The difference between the total cost of the goods repossessed (including
  • expenses) and the sale proceeds represents a profit or loss, which is transferred to the Profit and Loss
  • Account.
  • B) Partial Repossession ((2 marks))
  • In the case of partial repossession, the vendor takes back only a portion of the goods. The
  • repossessed portion is valued at an agreed value between the parties and debited to the Goods
  • Repossessed Account, while the same amount is credited to the Hire Purchaser’s Account. The
  • balance still due from the purchaser after such adjustment is either collected in cash or written off
  • as a loss.
questions.final_answer: Option Complete repossession ( (3 marks))
